- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment cools.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is falling, model often underestimates drop; add 1–2% buffer below trend.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); apply downward bias of 1–3% for first 5 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 75→70→68), model often holds too high; adjust forecast to align with 2–3 prior-day average if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- When sentiment is uniformly high (e.g., 1.00 for 3+ days), model may overfit recent trend; reduce forecast slope or add smoothing factor.
